chunks: And in the narration of Ṣafwān and Ibn al-Mughīrah, from someone who narrated it from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:

If the muḥṣan fornicator confesses, the first to stone him is the Imam, then the people. And if the evidence is established against him, the first to stone him is the witnesses, then the Imam, then the people.

key_terms.الزَّانِي الْمُحْصَنُ: a married fornicator liable to the fixed legal punishment of stoning
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the legitimate authority who leads the implementation of the legal punishment
key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةُ: the legal proof or witness-based evidence establishing the offense
key_terms.يَرْجُمُهُ: stones him as part of the prescribed punishment

ai.seo_question: Who begins the stoning punishment in cases proven by confession versus witnesses?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning the order of carrying out rajm in the case of a muḥṣan fornicator. It distinguishes between a case established by confession and one established by legal evidence, assigning a different order of participation in each case.
